--- .redfirst/env-down.sh ---
#!/bin/sh
# Generated by `redfirst init --hooks node-postgres-docker`.
#
# redfirst copies .redfirst/ out of the base branch and runs it there, so an
# edit on a branch under judgement changes nothing about how that branch is
# judged. Keep .redfirst/** in paths.protected and let a human review every
# change to it.
set -u
# No set -e: this hook runs on the panic path and on the deadline, when half
# the environment was never built, and stopping at the first command that finds
# nothing to stop would leak the rest. A non-zero exit here is exit code 2.

# --volumes: the data of this run leaves with it. The volume name carries the
# run id through COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, so this stops nobody else's database.
docker compose down --volumes --remove-orphans
--- .redfirst/env-reset.sh ---
#!/bin/sh
# Generated by `redfirst init --hooks node-postgres-docker`.
#
# redfirst copies .redfirst/ out of the base branch and runs it there, so an
# edit on a branch under judgement changes nothing about how that branch is
# judged. Keep .redfirst/** in paths.protected and let a human review every
# change to it.
set -eu

# Data only. The schema comes from the migrations, which sit in paths.protected,
# so the base tree and the head tree share it by construction; recreating it
# between runs would pay for a migration nothing changed.
#
# The bookkeeping table of the migration tool stays: emptying it would tell the
# next run the schema was never applied.
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U "$PGUSER" -d "$PGDATABASE" -q -c '
DO $$
DECLARE t text;
BEGIN
  FOR t IN
    SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables
    WHERE schemaname = ''public'' AND tablename NOT LIKE ''%migration%''
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format(''TRUNCATE TABLE %I CASCADE'', t);
  END LOOP;
END $$;'
--- .redfirst/env-up.sh ---
#!/bin/sh
# Generated by `redfirst init --hooks node-postgres-docker`.
#
# redfirst copies .redfirst/ out of the base branch and runs it there, so an
# edit on a branch under judgement changes nothing about how that branch is
# judged. Keep .redfirst/** in paths.protected and let a human review every
# change to it.
set -eu

# A missing toolchain is a broken repository, not a failing test, and this hook
# is where the difference can still be told: a non-zero exit here is exit code
# 2, while a non-zero exit from test.sh means the suite went red.
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
	echo "docker is not on PATH" >&2
	exit 1
}

docker compose up --detach --wait

# --wait returns once the healthcheck passes, so the compose file needs one on
# the database. Without it the first test run races the server's startup and
# the failure looks like the agent's.
--- .redfirst/env.sh ---
#!/bin/sh
# Generated by `redfirst init --hooks node-postgres-docker`.
#
# redfirst copies .redfirst/ out of the base branch and runs it there, so an
# edit on a branch under judgement changes nothing about how that branch is
# judged. Keep .redfirst/** in paths.protected and let a human review every
# change to it.

# One compose project per run id: two branches checked at once would otherwise
# fight over the same containers, networks and volumes. Compose derives all
# three names from this one variable.
COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME="redfirst-${REDFIRST_RUN_ID}"
export COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME

# The host port is whatever compose assigned, so the compose file has to publish
# 5432 without pinning a host port. A pinned port is a collision between two
# runs on one machine.
PGHOST=127.0.0.1
PGPORT=$(docker compose port postgres 5432 2>/dev/null | sed 's/.*://')
PGUSER=postgres
PGPASSWORD=postgres
PGDATABASE=app
export PGHOST PGPORT PGUSER PGPASSWORD PGDATABASE
export DATABASE_URL="postgres://${PGUSER}:${PGPASSWORD}@${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}/${PGDATABASE}"
--- .redfirst/test.sh ---
#!/bin/sh
# Generated by `redfirst init --hooks node-postgres-docker`.
#
# redfirst copies .redfirst/ out of the base branch and runs it there, so an
# edit on a branch under judgement changes nothing about how that branch is
# judged. Keep .redfirst/** in paths.protected and let a human review every
# change to it.
set -eu

# Once per phase: the working copy is shared by every run inside it, and the
# schema lives in the services, which outlive the copy.
if [ "$REDFIRST_PROBE_INDEX" = 1 ]; then
	pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
	pnpm migrate
fi

# $REDFIRST_FILTER is left unquoted on purpose: it carries a list of files, and
# an empty one has to run the whole suite. --no-cache keeps every probe honest.
pnpm exec vitest run --no-cache \
	--reporter=junit --outputFile="$REDFIRST_RESULTS" $REDFIRST_FILTER
